sets.title: A time I helped
sets.summary: Students write a short personal story about helping someone, practicing time-order words and past-tense verbs.

tasks.prompt: Think of a time you helped a friend or someone in your family. Write what happened first, next and last.

models.text: I help my sistr. Frst I get her shoo. Nex I tie. She hapy.
annotations: Names who was helped and tells three events in order.
Starts sentences with the time words Frst and Nex.
Short sentences repeat one pattern; invented spelling (sistr, shoo) shows the sounds the writer hears.

models.text: I helped my little sister. First she could not find her shoes for school. Next I looked under the bed and I find them. Last I tied her shoes because she is only four. She said thank you and I was happy.
annotations: Events go in order with First, Next and Last.
Uses because to give a reason.
Mostly past tense, with one slip (I find them).

models.text: Last Saturday I helped my little sister get ready for dance class. First, she could not find her shoes, so she started to cry. Next, I searched under the bed and found one shoe. Then I discovered the other one by the door! Finally, I tied the laces in double knots. My sister hugged me, and I felt proud.
annotations: Opens with when it happened and ends with how the writer felt.
Uses many time words (First, Next, Then, Finally) to connect events.
Joins ideas with so and and; past-tense verbs are correct.
Exact verbs like searched and discovered help the reader picture the story.

checklist.text: I told what happened first, next and last.
I wrote about things that already happened, like helped and found.
I used time words like first, next and last.

tasks.prompt: Write a story about a time you helped someone at school. Tell what the problem was, what you did, and how it ended. Add details so the reader can picture it.

models.text: A new boy. He no talk. I say hi. We play ball. He smil. Now frend.
annotations: Tells events in order with very short sentences.
Leaves out some verbs and endings (He no talk).
Uses everyday words to name people and actions.

models.text: One day at school a new boy came to our class. The problem was he did not know anybody and he sit alone at lunch. So I decided to say hi and ask him to play soccer at recess. After that we played every day. In the end he is my friend now. I felt good because he was happy.
annotations: Has a beginning, a problem, actions and an ending.
Uses So, After that and In the end to link events.
Some verb tense slips (he sit, he is my friend now).
Gives a reason with because.

models.text: In October, a new student named Tomás joined our class. At lunch he sat alone and stared at his tray, so I could tell he felt nervous. I invited him to sit with my friends and me. Then, at recess, we taught him our tag game, and he was the fastest runner! The next morning, Tomás waved at me when he walked in. Now we are good friends, and I am glad I was brave enough to say hello.
annotations: Clear beginning, middle and end that moves through time (In October, Then, The next morning, Now).
Mixes short and longer sentences joined with so, and and when.
Shows feelings through actions (stared at his tray) instead of only naming them.
Exact words like invited, nervous and brave.

checklist.text: My story has a problem, what I did, and an ending.
I used words like then, after that and in the end to move the story along.
Some of my sentences join two ideas with so, and, or because.
I used feeling words and action words that show what happened.

sets.title: How a seed grows
sets.summary: Students describe the stages of a bean plant's growth and what plants need, using science words and time-order signals.

tasks.prompt: Write about how a bean seed grows into a plant. Tell the steps in order.
frames: A seed needs ___ and ___ to grow.

models.text: The seed in dirt. Water. Roots come down. Leefs come up. Big plant.
annotations: Lists the steps in the right order.
Uses words and short phrases, some without verbs.
Uses the science words seed and roots.

models.text: First you put the seed in the soil and give it water. Next the roots grows down in the soil. Then a little stem come up and it has two leaves. At the end the bean plant is tall and green.
annotations: Steps are in order with First, Next, Then and At the end.
Connects ideas inside sentences with and.
Some verb errors (the roots grows, a stem come).

models.text: First, a bean seed is planted in moist soil. After a few days, the seed coat splits open and a tiny root pushes down into the soil. Next, a curved stem pokes up toward the light. Then, two leaves unfold, and the plant starts to make its own food from sunlight. Finally, it grows tall and makes new bean pods.
annotations: Every step builds on the one before it.
Adds time details like After a few days.
Exact science words: seed coat, moist, unfold.
Uses present tense correctly to tell about a process.

checklist.text: I put the steps in the order they happen.
Each step is a full sentence with a doing word.
I used plant words like seed, root, stem and leaves.

tasks.prompt: Write a short report about what plants need to live and grow. Tell at least three things plants need and what each one does for the plant.
frames: Plants need ___ to live and grow.

models.text: Plants need water. Plants need sun. Plants need dirt. Plant drink water.
annotations: Names three things plants need.
Repeats one sentence pattern (Plants need ___).
Uses simple, everyday words like dirt and drink.

models.text: Plants need three things to grow. They need water because the roots drink it. They need sun light to make food. Also they need soil so the roots can hold the plant. If a plant dont get water it will die. That is what plants need.
annotations: Has a topic sentence and a closing sentence.
Uses because, so and if to connect ideas.
Some spelling and grammar errors (sun light, dont get).

models.text: Plants need several things to stay alive and grow. First, they need water, which the roots soak up and carry to the leaves. Second, plants need sunlight because their leaves use light to make food. Third, they need air, especially a gas called carbon dioxide. Healthy soil also gives plants nutrients. Without these things, a plant will wilt and may die.
annotations: Topic sentence, details in order (First, Second, Third) and a closing idea.
Uses which and because to add information inside sentences.
Precise science words: nutrients, carbon dioxide, wilt.

checklist.text: I started with a topic sentence and ended with a closing sentence.
I used because, so or which to tell what each need does.
I used science words like sunlight, roots and nutrients.
I used order words like first, second and also.

sets.title: Sharing in equal groups
sets.summary: Students explain how they solve equal-group problems, using math words and because or so to show their thinking.

tasks.prompt: Maya has 12 crayons. She puts them into 3 equal groups. How many crayons are in each group? Explain how you know.

fields: My answer and how I know

models.text: 12 crayon. 3 group. 4 in group. I count.
annotations: Gives the correct answer.
Uses numbers and short phrases instead of full sentences.
Uses the math words group and count.

models.text: Each group has 4 crayons. First I draw 3 circles. Then I put one crayon in each circle until I have no more crayons. I know is 4 because 4 and 4 and 4 is 12.
annotations: States the answer, then tells the steps.
Uses First, Then and because to explain.
Some errors: past steps told with present verbs (I draw, I put) and a missing word (I know is 4).

models.text: Each group has 4 crayons. To solve it, I drew 3 circles for the groups. Then I passed out the crayons one at a time, like dealing cards, until all 12 were gone. Every circle had 4. I checked my answer by adding 4 + 4 + 4, and it equals 12, so my groups are equal.
annotations: Answer first, then the steps, then a check.
Joins ideas with until, and and so.
Exact math words: equal, equals, adding.
Compares the method to something familiar (dealing cards).

checklist.text: I wrote my answer and then the steps I used.
I used because or so to show how I know.
I used math words like equal, groups and each.

tasks.prompt: There are 20 students in a class. The teacher wants to make teams with the same number of students on each team. Explain two different ways she could make equal teams and why each way works.
frames: One way is to make ___ teams of ___.
This also works because ___ times ___ equals 20.

annotations: Gives two correct ways.
Uses numbers and short phrases.
Does not yet say why each way works.

models.text: One way is to make 4 teams of 5 students. This works because 5 and 5 and 5 and 5 is 20. Another way is 2 teams with 10 students. This work because 10 plus 10 is 20. All the teams has the same number so it is fair.
annotations: Gives two ways and a reason for each.
Uses the frame This works because ___ to link each answer to its reason.
Some agreement errors (This work, the teams has).

models.text: The teacher could make 4 teams with 5 students on each team. This works because 4 groups of 5 is 20, so nobody is left out. Another way is to make 5 teams of 4. It also works, since 5 × 4 equals 20, just like 4 × 5. I checked both ways by skip counting by fives and by fours. Each time I landed exactly on 20, so the teams are equal.
annotations: Explains each way, then tells how the answer was checked.
Uses because, since and so to show cause and effect.
Exact math language: groups of, equals, skip counting.
Notices a pattern (5 × 4 is like 4 × 5).

checklist.text: I explained two ways, and I told why each one works.
I used because, since or so to connect my answer and my reason.
I used math words like equal, groups of, times and equals.
